newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products gain on aggressive buying, future.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products gain on aggressive buying, future.

text.p: NWE oil products all gained on Tuesday, with gasoline and fuel oil helped by aggressive physical buying, dealers said.
Gasoline barges rose some $3 a tonne as Eurograde barges traded at $202.50, $203.00 and $203.50 fob ARA. The buyer and seller were the same in each case, dealers said.
Traders said they felt the market would more naturally have risen by $1/$2 were it not for the aggressive buying.
High sulphur fuel oil also saw keen buying, in this case from two players, a trading house and a major. Deals were concluded at $92 fob Antwerp and fob Rotterdam, up $2.
Bunker demand was average, suppliers said.

The heating oil barge market was, by contrast, short of buying. Prices rose by around $3 a tonne as IPE March futures strengthened, but premiums sagged from some higher fob Rotterdam levels concluded on Monday.
Prompt offers were at IPE March +$1 fob ARA. Demand in Germany was light as spring-like weather persisted. Higher prices further discouraged buyers.
One diesel barge trade was concluded at IPE March +$13.50.
